trajectories.name: Gift → Rupture → Restoration
trajectories.description: Something precious is given, then broken, then recovered in a deeper way. The pattern of grace interrupted and returned.

movements.name: Gift Reception
movements.description: The soul receives something it did not earn and could not achieve alone.
movements.internalMovement: Gratitude awakens. The heart recognizes dependence. Wonder opens the soul.

movements.name: Rupture: Loss
movements.description: The gift is withdrawn or broken. Loss reveals how deeply the soul had relied upon it.
movements.internalMovement: Denial, grief, confusion. The soul learns it cannot hold what is not ultimately its own.

movements.name: Restoration: Deeper
movements.description: The gift returns, but transformed. The soul receives it again with deeper humility and truer understanding.
movements.internalMovement: Renewed gratitude, purified desire, transformed relationship to the gift.

tensions.name: Attachment vs Detachment
tensions.description: The tension between holding the gift close and letting it go freely.

tensions.name: Possession vs Trust
tensions.description: Do I own the gift or does it own me? Is my security in what I hold or in God's faithfulness?

trajectories.fulfillment: Christ is the gift given and received. His death is our rupture; His resurrection is our restoration, transformed and eternal.
trajectories.liturgicalConnection: Eucharist: bread broken and given, received and transformed.

trajectories.name: Guilt → Offering → Surrender → Union
trajectories.description: From the weight of sin to the freedom of self-gift. The soul moves from shame to offering itself to God and, finally, to union.

movements.name: Guilt: Recognition
movements.description: The soul recognizes its sin. Not mere regret, but true recognition of separation from God.
movements.internalMovement: Shame, contrition, dawning awareness of need for God.

movements.name: Offering: Reparation
movements.description: The soul seeks to make amends. It offers itself in small acts, prayers, sacrifices.
movements.internalMovement: Desire to restore, to give back, to repair what was broken.

movements.name: Surrender: Self-Gift
movements.description: The soul moves beyond individual acts to offering itself wholly. No longer seeking to earn, but to give.
movements.internalMovement: Willingness to be given, to be used, to belong entirely to God.
movements.externalSign: Vows, committed love, abandonment to God's will.

movements.name: Union: Transformed
movements.description: The soul, having given itself, finds that it is held in God's love. Union replaces separation. Self-gift becomes divine embrace.
movements.internalMovement: Deep peace, intimate knowledge of being loved, transformation into God's image.

tensions.name: Shame vs Grace
tensions.description: Can I be loved despite my sin? Or does guilt separate me forever?

tensions.name: Earning vs Receiving
tensions.description: Do I have to earn God's love back, or is it already given?

tensions.name: Self-Loss vs Self-Finding
tensions.description: To surrender myself—is this annihilation or true freedom?

trajectories.fulfillment: Christ is the guilt-bearer. His sacrifice is our offering. His love is our surrender. Union with Him is our final fulfillment.
trajectories.liturgicalConnection: Reconciliation: from guilt to absolution to renewed communion.

trajectories.name: Command → Failure → Love
trajectories.description: From obedience to law to the discovery that love fulfills what law demands. The soul learns the freedom beyond mere rule-keeping.

movements.name: Command: Hearing
movements.description: The soul receives God's command. It is clear, demanding, non-negotiable.
movements.internalMovement: Clarity, resolve, determination to obey. The soul is alive to duty.

movements.name: Failure: Discovery
movements.description: The soul strives to keep the command and discovers it cannot. Law reveals human weakness.
movements.internalMovement: Frustration, humility, growing awareness of need for grace beyond human effort.

movements.name: Love: Awakening
movements.description: In failure, the soul discovers that love is what God actually seeks. Love is the fulfillment of the law.
movements.internalMovement: Shift from fear and striving to trust and desire. The heart awakens to God's love.
movements.externalSign: Joy, freedom, spontaneous goodness flowing from love rather than duty.

tensions.name: Law vs Grace
tensions.description: Does God demand or invite? Is He judge or lover?

tensions.name: Striving vs Resting
tensions.description: Must I constantly earn God's favor, or can I rest in His love?

trajectories.fulfillment: Christ fulfills the law through love. His command is His love. In Him, duty becomes desire.
trajectories.liturgicalConnection: The New Commandment: love one another as I have loved you.

trajectories.name: Control → Collapse → Service
trajectories.description: From the illusion of mastery to the surrender of control to the joy of service. The soul learns that power is given, not seized.

movements.name: Control: Illusion
movements.description: The soul believes itself master of its fate. It builds, plans, controls outcomes.
movements.internalMovement: Confidence, self-reliance, perhaps pride. The soul feels strong.

movements.name: Collapse: Loss
movements.description: Plans fail. Illness strikes. Death nears. The soul discovers it controls nothing ultimately.
movements.internalMovement: Fear, despair, then gradually, acceptance. The illusion shatters.

movements.name: Service: Liberation
movements.description: Freed from the burden of control, the soul discovers the joy of serving. Power is received and used for others.
movements.internalMovement: Freedom, lightness, purpose. The soul finds deep joy in obedience and service.
movements.externalSign: Care for others, humility, gladness, fruitfulness.

tensions.name: Power vs Powerlessness
tensions.description: Who is truly powerful: the one who commands or the one who serves?

tensions.name: Self-Will vs God's Will
tensions.description: Can my will and God's will be one? Or are they always in tension?

trajectories.fulfillment: Christ emptied Himself to serve. His power is revealed in His surrender. In Him, true greatness is found in humility and service.
trajectories.liturgicalConnection: The washing of feet: Christ models power through service.

trajectories.name: Bondage → Liberation → Freedom
trajectories.description: From slavery to sin to the experience of being freed to the joy of true freedom in Christ. A movement of increasing liberation.

movements.name: Bondage: Awareness
movements.description: The soul recognizes it is enslaved. Not free to choose the good. Bound to patterns, desires, fears.
movements.internalMovement: Growing despair that change is possible. The soul feels trapped.
movements.externalSign: Repetition of sin, inability to stop, desperation.

movements.name: Liberation: Rescue
movements.description: God acts. The chains are broken. The soul is freed from the power of sin.
movements.internalMovement: Joy, amazement, gratitude. The soul discovers it can choose anew.
movements.externalSign: Conversion, radical life change, new capacity for good.

movements.name: Freedom: Maturity
movements.description: Not mere freedom from bondage, but freedom for—to love, to create, to be fully alive in God.
movements.internalMovement: Deep peace, authentic desire for good, spontaneous love.
movements.externalSign: Holiness, joy, apostolic effectiveness, love of others.

tensions.name: Slavery vs Freedom
tensions.description: Is the soul truly enslaved, or does it willingly choose captivity?

tensions.name: Despair vs Hope
tensions.description: Can I be freed? Does liberation exist, or is it an illusion?

trajectories.fulfillment: Christ is our liberation. His death breaks the chains of sin and death. In His resurrection, we are freed to live as God's children.
trajectories.liturgicalConnection: Baptism: dying and rising with Christ, freed from sin, born to new life.

trajectories.name: Ignorance → Illumination
trajectories.description: From darkness of not knowing God to the light of divine knowledge. The soul moves from blindness to vision.

movements.name: Ignorance: Darkness
movements.description: The soul does not know God. It may mistake other things for God. It stumbles in darkness.
movements.internalMovement: Confusion, seeking without finding, false answers, spiritual emptiness.

movements.name: Illumination: Awakening
movements.description: God reveals Himself. The soul begins to see truth. Light breaks into darkness.
movements.internalMovement: Wonder, awe, recognition. The soul sees what it had always missed.

tensions.name: Darkness vs Light
tensions.description: Am I truly blind, or do I just resist the light?

trajectories.fulfillment: Christ is the Light of the World. In Him, we see the Father. Illumination is the gift of His Spirit.
trajectories.liturgicalConnection: Baptism: from darkness to light; from ignorance to incorporation in Christ.

trajectories.name: Distance → Presence → Communion
trajectories.description: From the ache of distance from God to the experience of His presence to intimate union. A progressive drawing near.

movements.name: Distance: Yearning
movements.description: The soul feels separated from God. It yearns for what it does not yet possess. Longing becomes its prayer.
movements.internalMovement: Ache, desire, seeking. The soul knows something is missing.

movements.name: Presence: Encounter
movements.description: God draws near. The distance collapses. The soul experiences God's presence with immediacy.
movements.internalMovement: Joy, peace, certainty. The soul knows it is not alone.

movements.name: Communion: Union
movements.description: Presence becomes communion. The soul and God are no longer merely near each other; they are united. Mutual indwelling.
movements.internalMovement: Deep peace, identity transformed, continuous awareness of union.

tensions.name: Distance vs Closeness
tensions.description: Is the distance real or illusion? Is God truly absent or only hidden?

tensions.name: Seeking vs Finding
tensions.description: Does the search ever end? Does presence satisfy longing or deepen it?

trajectories.fulfillment: In Christ, distance is abolished. He is Emmanuel—God with us. The Spirit indwells believers. Ultimate communion awaits the vision of God.
trajectories.liturgicalConnection: The Eucharist: Christ's real presence; communion with God and the Church.

trajectories.name: Calling → Resistance → Fidelity
trajectories.description: From hearing God's call to the struggle to answer to the perseverance of faithful love. The soul learns to say 'yes' and keep saying it.

movements.name: Calling: Summons
movements.description: God calls. The soul hears itself named, invited, chosen for something beyond itself.
movements.internalMovement: Awe, awareness of being known and chosen. The soul feels summoned to something true.

movements.name: Resistance: Struggle
movements.description: The cost becomes apparent. Resistance rises: fear, doubt, the weight of sacrifice. The soul must choose again.
movements.internalMovement: Fear, doubt, inner conflict. The soul tastes the cost of yes.
movements.externalSign: Struggle, near-abandonment, tears, nights of darkness.

movements.name: Fidelity: Perseverance
movements.description: The soul chooses yes, again and again. Love becomes perseverance. Calling becomes lived covenant.
movements.internalMovement: Deep commitment, quiet strength, joy mixed with sorrow, transparent obedience.
movements.externalSign: Perseverance, fruit, sacrifice borne with grace, love that endures.

tensions.name: Acceptance vs Resistance
tensions.description: Am I clinging to my own will, or have I truly accepted God's will?

tensions.name: Cost vs Reward
tensions.description: What am I willing to lose? What do I receive in return?

trajectories.fulfillment: Christ is the perfect model of faithful answering to His Father. His 'yes' in Gethsemane becomes His redemptive yes on the cross.
trajectories.liturgicalConnection: Religious profession: total commitment to God's calling in Christ.
